biography.plain_text: Lionel Masson is a French pharmacist and co-founder of Pharmacie Lafayette. He moved from Marseille to Toulouse in 1995, buying a pharmacy with Jean-Michel Wurfel and developing a national network. The partners sold a majority stake to Five Arrows Principal Investments in 2016, initially retaining minority interests in the business.

long_biography.plain_text:
Lower prices for everyday pharmacy purchases were central to Lionel Masson’s approach at Pharmacie Lafayette. He began with vitamin C, then reduced prices on contraceptive pills after recognising how much of the pharmacy’s trade came from women. His model combined affordable products with a broad choice and advice from qualified pharmacists.

The network also gave affiliated pharmacies access to agreements with manufacturers, widening the range they could offer. Its central team helped members with premises, shop layout and marketing. Pharmacies joined through an assistance agreement, paying royalties for the brand and a percentage of their turnover.
